facts.subject: KILN-004
facts.fact: KILN-004 was opened on 2026-10-21 10:27 to inventory the merged system and decide how to separate it again into reusable pieces; the Kiln server it inventories had been running on 127.0.0.1:5380 (PID 22866, cwd apps/server) since 2026-10-20 23:46.

facts.subject: playback-kiln-002 branch
facts.fact: Example C lives on Playback branch perf/kiln-002-redaction-mask-post in /Volumes/SSD/code/playback-kiln-002: cdfb0d8c9 (2026-10-20 13:31, 13 files, +4401/−28) adds REDACTION_MASK_POST=kiln and ac835daa9 (14:25) re-vendors the launcher; the docker-compose.yml default line (REDACTION_MASK_POST cpu) is uncommitted because pre-commit cannot pass on macOS.

facts.subject: KILN-004 agent E
facts.fact: Agent E (history) was stopped by a usage limit before its synthesis was written; the orchestrator committed its scratch notes unreviewed in 1d0c894 and agent E completed them afterwards.

facts.subject: KILN-001 D10
facts.fact: KILN-001 decided that CUDA runs through the runner as a subprocess, locally or over SSH, not through the runner's HTTP server, because that 'removes a network-exposed code-execution endpoint; reuses SSH authentication for remote hosts'.

facts.subject: KILN-001 D3
facts.fact: KILN-001 decided on SHA-256 everywhere instead of cyrb53 (weakness P-5: cyrb53 identities in fields named *_sha256); Phase 8 then kept cyrb53 bit-for-bit because Perf Lab's store and routes are keyed by it.

facts.subject: KILN-001 D1
facts.fact: KILN-001 based the unified workbench on Kiln's UI and compiler and turned Perf Lab's evidence model into a headless package (@kiln/evidence); Perf Lab's app stayed a read-only reference.

facts.subject: KILN-001 D6
facts.fact: KILN-001: hardware evidence overrides the cost model in compiler decisions only when confidence intervals separate (decide.evidence v2, minReps 3).

facts.subject: KILN-001 record
facts.fact: KILN-001 chose the measurement record as the unification point between Kiln and Perf Lab: 'The cleanest unification point is the record'.

facts.subject: KILN-001 protocol rules
facts.fact: KILN-001 moved repetitionOrder and the output check into @kiln/evidence/src/protocol.ts because 'Two copies held equal by a test is one rule with two chances to drift'.

facts.subject: KILN-001 Phase 8 scope
facts.fact: KILN-001 left lab job execution out of Phase 8 (the done-condition needs only imported data): Kiln's /api/lab answers 501 to creating, approving or cancelling a lab job.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-003 §5
facts.fact: ML-PERF-003 chose option B, an SSH container executor run from the Mac, over A (lab on the DGX) and C (an agent service on the DGX); a job's lifetime is tied to its SSH connection on purpose because 'an orphaned GPU process on a shared host is worse than a cancelled job', with C kept as the better trade if jobs grow to hours.

facts.subject: KILN-003 driver API
facts.fact: KILN-003 v2 replaced the local and SSH transports with one HTTP driver API on every host, explicitly reversing ML-PERF-003 §5 ('this design takes the agent and drops SSH'), and states 'The API has no authentication, by decision (2026-10-20)'.

facts.subject: KILN-003 user direction
facts.fact: The user directed KILN-003 mid-guide to 'simplify, unify… losing functionality is fine', which produced the nine-noun model (§11) and the removal table (§12.2), and chose 'plain TCP… a local HTTP server too… leave authentication out' for the driver.

facts.subject: KILN-003 removals
facts.fact: KILN-003 §12.2 removes executors.json/CudaRunnerExecutor, install-runner-over-SSH, kiln_runner.py serve, runner --ncu, kiln-docker-python, Perf Lab's Mac process executor and uv env, synthetic hosts and seeding, the second job system, and cyrb53; 49f5156 deleted the executors, jobs.ts, lab probe.ts, lab seed/job/host/evidence routes, kiln-docker-python and fake-runner.mjs.

facts.subject: KILN-003 principles
facts.fact: KILN-003's rules: the driver runs steps and never interprets them; a collector declares what it disturbs (ncu runs never contribute latencies); everything that can change a measurement is part of identity; conditions describe a run but never enter its identity.

facts.subject: KILN-003 GPU lock
facts.fact: The KILN-003 GPU lock is an advisory flock in /run/lock (not /tmp, which systemd-tmpfiles ages), one per GPU UUID; CPU jobs on a GPU host also take it so GPU jobs cannot disturb their timing.

facts.subject: KILN-003 environments
facts.fact: KILN-003 has two environment kinds, container (pinned by image ID) and host, with 'deliberately no virtual-environment variant'; Perf Lab's uv venv became the perf-lab-cpu container.

facts.subject: lab.js .agent()
facts.fact: Program-declared agents (.agent()) were removed from lab.js on 2026-10-12 by the second-consumer test in favour of one built-in assistant, because per-program agents 'added configuration without adding evidence'.

facts.subject: Perf Lab runner
facts.fact: Perf Lab runs one job and one process at a time on host local 'because concurrent benchmark processes would measure each other', interleaves arms per repetition with a seeded order, and imports failed processes as invalid runs.

facts.subject: Perf Lab offline capture
facts.fact: Offline, a Perf Lab local capture fails rather than being simulated, because simulating it would mint synthetic evidence for a host that measures for real.

facts.subject: Perf Lab spec hash check
facts.fact: The Perf Lab server re-hashes every submitted capture spec and refuses a mismatch with 409 spec_hash_mismatch.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-002 public media
facts.fact: ML-PERF-002 admits only privacy 'public' media into the lab (column constraint plus a route re-check), making 'a private frame was served by the lab' impossible rather than discouraged.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-002 archives
facts.fact: ML-PERF-002 decided that evidence archives are captures, not uploads of runs: imports go through plan status import and approved jobs so hash identity and provenance hold.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-002 matching port
facts.fact: ML-PERF-002 computes detection matches at import in TypeScript and pins equivalence with the Python by a golden test: 'Two implementations must stay equal; the golden test is the enforcement seam'.

facts.subject: KILN-002 PE
facts.fact: KILN-002's kiln-paired/1 importer (task PE) is blocked because the importer belongs in Perf Lab's lab-workbench/server/runner.ts, which is 'imported verbatim; never edited in this repository'.

facts.subject: KILN-002 lab execution
facts.fact: KILN-002 kept lab job execution out of scope ('three examples with different runtimes … would each need their own executor first') and routed results through kiln-paired/1 evidence archives instead — the gap KILN-003 took on.

facts.subject: KILN-002 Example B
facts.fact: KILN-002 did not build B2–B5 (the W-27 motion-grey kernel) because B1 refuted gray-is-worth-a-kernel; the cost is in videoconvert NV12→RGB, which belongs to factory-videos.

facts.subject: KILN-002 permission rule
facts.fact: KILN-002: reaching a GPU host over SSH requires explicit permission each time.

facts.subject: KILN-002 shipped schedules
facts.fact: KILN-002 kept Example C's shipped program set as exported (rtx5090 schedules) after finding they beat the schedules chosen under the measured gb10 spec (2,190 vs 4,734 µs over five W-28 kernels).

facts.subject: KILN-001 agent sandbox
facts.fact: KILN-001 moved agent eval from a sandboxed frame to a worker reached only through a MessagePort because 'Nothing in the CSP or the sandbox attribute stops a frame from navigating itself'; agent-written scripts are held until the user presses Run.

facts.subject: KILN-001 model gateway
facts.fact: KILN-001's model gateway is a stateless relay (one upstream call per request, one llm_calls row); 'The page runs the tool loop, not the server'.

facts.subject: remote GPU execution
facts.fact: Remote execution changed shape four times in nine days: ML-PERF-003 SSH executor (designed 10-12), KILN-001 SSH runner executors (built 10-19), KILN-003 v1 local+ssh transports (10-20 20:18), KILN-003 v2 HTTP driver (20:41); the deployment then reaches bling's driver through an ssh -N -L tunnel on 127.0.0.1:5481, outside the core.

facts.subject: remote GPU execution
facts.fact: The unauthenticated KILN-003 driver re-introduces the network-reachable code-execution endpoint that KILN-001 D10 removed; it is mitigated only by binding to 127.0.0.1 (default --listen 127.0.0.1:5281) or Tailscale.

facts.subject: capture identity
facts.fact: Every KILN-003 capture has two identities: a SHA-256 of kiln-capture/1 canonical JSON (packages/exec/src/identity.ts) that keys catalog rows, and a cyrb53 lab_hash that lab programs look up (apps/server/src/db.ts:248-252, packages/exec/src/lab-hash.ts).

facts.subject: cyrb53
facts.fact: KILN-003 §12.2 retires cyrb53, but 8276bf7 moved it into the new core as packages/exec/src/lab-hash.ts ('kept because it is the identity every existing Perf Lab artifact and program uses').

facts.subject: synthetic hosts
facts.fact: Synthetic hosts were to be removed by KILN-003 (§12.2, task P4) but 8276bf7 keeps them as the fallback; packages/lab/src/data/capabilities.ts still holds 'NVIDIA GB10 (synthetic)' and 'RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (synthetic)' reports.

facts.subject: CPU lab runs on the Mac
facts.fact: KILN-003 §12.2 listed CPU-only lab runs on the Mac as a deliberate loss, but 8276bf7 restored them the same evening as kind perf-lab-sampler/1 in a perf-lab-cpu container behind a Mac driver on 127.0.0.1:5381; the guide was not updated.

facts.subject: kiln-probe/1
facts.fact: KILN-003 task P1 is ticked and names a kiln-probe/1 kind, but packages/exec/src/kinds/ holds only kiln-kernels.ts and perf-lab-sampler.ts; the string kiln-probe/1 appears only as the probe binary's output format in runner/docker/kiln-probe.cu:174.

facts.subject: ncu and nsys collectors
facts.fact: KILN-003 P2 (ncu and nsys collectors) is open, yet packages/exec/src/collectors/ncu.ts, nsys.ts and apps/server/src/exec/nsys-sqlite.ts exist; no host has run them because GPU counters need NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0 and a reboot on bling.

facts.subject: corresponds_to
facts.fact: The entity-graph edge corresponds_to, proposed by the memo and planned as KILN-001 Phase 8d (still unticked), is emitted by KILN-003 code for kernel captures (packages/exec/src/runs.ts:57) and nsys kernels (packages/exec/src/collectors/nsys.ts:42); no board reads kernel captures' runs yet.

facts.subject: runner/test/test_driver.py
facts.fact: KILN-003 §33.2 planned runner/test/test_driver.py; it does not exist, and the driver is exercised through apps/server/test with a fake docker and nvidia-smi.

facts.fact: KILN-001's 'Vault report after major milestones' box is unchecked although three vault reports were pushed (534ff7f, 43572ed, 4fc3320).

facts.fact: The KILN-003 guide predates what was built: it has no perf-lab-sampler/1, says cyrb53 is replaced (l.703) and Mac CPU runs are lost (l.697), and shows bling's driver on the LAN at 5281 (l.2157-2158).

facts.subject: KILN-003 scripts
facts.fact: KILN-003's P1 acceptance script 01-verify-measure-context.mjs still selects device server:spark on port 5280, both deleted in KILN-003 Steps 3–4.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-003 guide
facts.fact: ML-PERF-003's guide calls the capture hash 'a SHA-256 hash'; Perf Lab's code uses cyrb53 (src/lang/util.ts:1).

facts.subject: Perf Lab README
facts.fact: Perf Lab's README still says the workbench runs 'entirely on synthetic data' (l.25-29), contradicting l.126-135, and says nine programs where there are 11.

facts.subject: Perf Lab backend design
facts.fact: ML-PERF-001's backend design says 'three migrations'; Perf Lab has five by the end of ML-PERF-002.

facts.subject: sqlite readOnly
facts.fact: Opening Perf Lab's WAL SQLite store with {readOnly: true} rebuilds -shm in place when no writer is attached; Kiln's readers open a temporary copy of the db and -wal instead ('readOnly describes what SQL may do, not what happens to the files').

facts.subject: lab capture hash normal form
facts.fact: 877c273: stableStringify writes undefined as null while JSON.stringify drops the key, so imported runs were stored under 1c2ee7b51bf704 while the page looked for 21477f7f5fa54; the fix hashes the lowered JSON normal form, asserted for every preset capture.

facts.subject: Evidence Forget
facts.fact: The Kiln Evidence view's Forget deleted 9 of 11 jobs' records on bling, unrecoverably (KILN-002 Step 15).

facts.subject: run-on-gpu-host.sh
facts.fact: run-on-gpu-host.sh's KNOWN-FLAKY verdict (every revision failure also fails at least once at baseline) cannot detect a test that fails more often at the revision.

facts.subject: docker group
facts.fact: Supplementary groups are fixed when a process starts, so a user added to the docker group must re-login or use sg docker; learned in KILN-002 and hit again in KILN-003.

facts.subject: Perf Lab assistant
facts.fact: Perf Lab's assistant system prompt never arrived through lunaroute because pi-ai sends a developer role, which the gateway drops (the model answered with 48 input tokens); fixed with compat.supportsDeveloperRole = false.

facts.subject: Perf Lab run identity
facts.fact: Perf Lab runs keyed by experiment/arm/mode#rep re-pointed the 2,048-query rows when the plan ran at 1,024 queries; migration 3 keyed runs by (capture hash, rep). 'The end-to-end test found the most serious defect of the day, invisible to the unit tests'.

facts.subject: ML-PERF-002 golden port
facts.fact: The TypeScript port of PR 1005's matching first failed 26 of 28 golden cases because Python's compare_ground_truth pops matched_gt_ids as a side effect.

facts.subject: Perf Lab stale server
facts.fact: A stale Perf Lab server ran evidence captures as synthetic and minted 28 synthetic artifacts, deleted by hand with SQL; the /health features handshake was added so a stale server blocks evidence captures. 'A long-running server is part of the system under test'.

facts.subject: Perf Lab lab.js eval
facts.fact: Perf Lab evaluates lab programs and assistant code with unsandboxed new Function, which its author calls 'not acceptable for a shared deployment'.

facts.subject: X-Kiln-Proposer
facts.fact: Kiln's X-Kiln-Proposer header is self-declared: any holder of the session token can approve a job; it becomes enforceable only with the agent's own credential.

facts.subject: model gateway
facts.fact: Kiln's model gateway has no upstream timeout and no concurrency cap (recorded as a follow-up in KILN-001).

facts.subject: POST /api/lab/evidence
facts.fact: Kiln's POST /api/lab/evidence {path} reveals the contents of a tar archive the user names on the server's filesystem.

facts.subject: glossary: lab.js program
facts.fact: A plain-JS fluent builder returning lab(title), evaluated with new Function and compiled through expand, resolve, trace, validate, lower and plan passes into a serializable IR of experiments, arms, captures, imports, derives, params, hypotheses and boards.

facts.subject: glossary: capture (Perf Lab)
facts.fact: One experiment × arm × mode with a lowered spec and a cyrb53 hash; modes timing, trace, kernels, memory, cpu, sanitizer, later stages, predictions and tests.

facts.subject: glossary: capture (KILN-003)
facts.fact: Workload variant × mode × collectors × protocol × host; its identity kiln-capture/1 excludes the host's name so renaming a host does not change what was measured.

facts.subject: glossary: parameter binding
facts.fact: A lab.js parameter's phase (plan, data or view) is inferred from its strongest reader; plan-bound values enter the content hash and their changes produce a pending plan that never executes by itself.

facts.subject: glossary: provenance classes
facts.fact: observed | derived | heuristic | illustrative | unknown; missing is never zero; observed values are import-only and sealed (ProvenanceError).

facts.subject: glossary: verdict
facts.fact: Hypothesis verdicts are supported | refuted | open | unqualified; open while any predicted row is missing, unqualified when a supporting run failed validity; KILN-001 moved the function into @kiln/evidence (D12).

facts.subject: glossary: content id
facts.fact: Kiln's content id hashes canonical kernel source (entry symbol replaced), launch, input seeds and shapes; made independent of kernel names in Phase 4b; kiln-codegen/N is part of it, so a bump makes every older record stale.

facts.subject: glossary: evidenceId and cudaDevice
facts.fact: Kiln records key on a device's evidenceId (fingerprint-derived); cudaDevice derives one id per GPU from hostname and GPU UUID because 'The route is not a property of the GPU'.

facts.subject: glossary: measurePaired
facts.fact: Compiles one kernel under two pinned rows and measures both in one protocol run so both sides see the same clock state; records share a pairId and ev.ratio zips them per repetition.

facts.subject: glossary: eight-step loop
facts.fact: KILN-002's loop: measure, decide with a written hypothesis, write the program, check against the consumer's reference, integrate behind a switch, paired compare, consumer quality gate, record with identity.

facts.subject: glossary: identity suffix
facts.fact: Kiln kernels exported to consumers carry their identity in the emitted symbol k_<name>__<identity>, which lets a trace kernel be linked to its Kiln kernel by a corresponds_to edge (method symbol-suffix).

facts.subject: glossary: workload kind
facts.fact: A @kiln/exec module that knows one way of running code: validate, contentId, stage, lower (per repetition) and import.

facts.subject: glossary: collector
facts.fact: A KILN-003 module that observes runs, with a shape (wrapper, in-process or sidecar) and a disturbs list; a run contributes samples of a quantity only if no collector in its set disturbs it.

facts.subject: glossary: facts and offers
facts.fact: KILN-003 probes host facts and derives offers with blocked reasons into kiln-capabilities/1 documents ('facts are probed, offers are derived').

facts.subject: glossary: conditions
facts.fact: Run context such as co-tenants and utilisation, attached to every run but never part of its identity or validity (KILN-003 §22.5, from ML-PERF-003).

facts.subject: glossary: HostDevice
facts.fact: The Kiln page's device host:<id> for a driver host; it adopts the evidence device that the host's records name.

facts.subject: glossary: record context
facts.fact: {preset, project, params, script} stored on kiln-measure/1 records at compile time so records travel with what produced them (KILN-002 task RC).

facts.subject: glossary: held script
facts.fact: An agent-written script in Kiln waits in wb.pending until the user presses Run; a call made while one is held throws HeldScriptError.

facts.subject: glossary: evidence archive
facts.fact: A .tar.gz registered by SHA-256 under .data/evidence and imported through plan status import by a lab program that names it (ML-PERF-002).

facts.subject: Perf Lab sampler (M1 Pro CPU)
facts.fact: torch.compile of the deformable-attention sampler is slower than eager on the M1 Pro CPU: paired median ratio 2.58× (CI 2.18–2.69) on the first run, 2.50× (2.37–2.72) after the run-identity fix at 2,048 queries and 2.29× (1.88–2.52) at 1,024; compile-removes-intermediate refuted.

facts.subject: PR 1005 on dgx
facts.fact: Imported dgx archive verdicts for Grounding DINO PR 1005: outputs-exact supported (512/512), latency-halved refuted (reduction 0.303, CI [0.301, 0.306]), memory-within-20 refuted (warm cgroup +25.5 % / +23.2 %), prompt-reuse and fusion-active supported.

facts.subject: PR 1005 local CPU
facts.fact: The real DINO backend at both revisions on the M1 Pro CPU (FP32, 16 images, 32 paired requests, all outputs bitwise identical): 1,665 ms vs 1,654 ms medians; cpu-parts-preserve supported.

facts.subject: W-05 paired WebGPU
facts.fact: KILN-001's Phase 6 done-condition on the M1 Pro: W-05 thread vs row ratio 0.0079 [0.0072, 0.0083], n=7, 6.2 s; W-05 moved from open to supported.

facts.subject: WebGPU timer on M1 Pro
facts.fact: Chrome's WebGPU timestamps on the M1 Pro are quantised to 65.536 µs without --enable-unsafe-webgpu (1 ns with it), and GPU clock levels make unpaired runs differ up to ~3× for the same code.

facts.subject: check:pl
facts.fact: @kiln/lab reproduces Perf Lab's local-sampler speedup bit-for-bit (2.4964× [2.3744, 2.7211], n=4) and every hash, lint, number and verdict; all 37 differing leaves are additions or relabels.

facts.subject: lab:import
facts.fact: lab:import moved Perf Lab's store (1 dataset, 1 archive, 128 media, 70 artifacts, 80 runs, 12 jobs) into Kiln in 0.38 s; 157 of 158 /api/lab responses were identical to Perf Lab's server.

facts.subject: Example A
facts.fact: Example A on the M1 Pro: GPU/CPU 0.029 [0.024, 0.031] at 1,385×768; GPU plus ImageData paint 75.9 ms at 2,297×768; gpu-rebuild-1385 and cap-lift-interactive supported; quality gate max |Δ| 2.2e-6.

facts.subject: Example B1
facts.fact: B1 on the M1 Pro: grey conversion is 9.3 % of the session against a 20 % bar; single-threaded videoconvert NV12→RGB costs 4.4–4.94 ms/frame against 0.49 ms VideoToolbox decode; gray-is-worth-a-kernel refuted.

facts.subject: W-28 exactness
facts.fact: W-28 mask post-processing is bit-exact with Playback's CPU loop: 0 of 67,272,192 reference pixels on three platforms and 0 of 269,352,960 kernel pixels over 120 runs.

facts.subject: W-28 on dgx
facts.fact: On dgx (GB10) the Kiln mask path is 6.8× faster than the CPU loop for 100 masks at 768×416 (3.340 vs 22.626 ms); CUDA init 0.257 s, load() 1.687 s.

facts.subject: C4 on bling
facts.fact: With REDACTION_MASK_POST=kiln on bling every correctness gate passes but whole-service throughput is 0.974 / 0.971 / 0.968 of baseline at concurrency 1/4/8 (repeat 0.987 / 0.958 / 0.964); infer_preprocess rises ~3.1 ms/frame; gb10-unchanged-or-better refuted; the ground-truth gate does not exercise the GPU path.

facts.subject: Kiln cost model on GB10
facts.fact: Kiln's analytic model over-predicts W-28 on the GB10 by 6.6–115× because a gather whose stride is not constant is billed as uncoalesced (129 MB charged where 13.5 MB is essential).

facts.subject: kiln-probe on bling
facts.fact: kiln-probe on an idle DGX Spark (bling): 258–259 GB/s read, 28.92 TFLOP/s FMA, 2.37–2.40 µs launch; on dgx with co-tenants read bandwidth is 19 % lower (205.6–209.4 GB/s).

facts.subject: perf-lab-sampler/1 on two hosts
facts.fact: KILN-003 sampler compiled ÷ eager: Mac 1.43× (1.26–1.60), bling 1.08× (1.07–1.12); the Mac's ratio drifted 1.57 / 1.68 / 1.43 / 1.45 across sessions ('A within-session interval does not cover the next session').

facts.subject: KILN-003 job latency
facts.fact: A KILN-003 kernel job takes 13–18 s from Measure to records; four jobs on two hosts finished in 65 s.

facts.subject: dgx host
facts.fact: dgx (playback@dgx, gx10-b2d2, ASUS GX10): NVIDIA GB10, CC 12.1, driver 580.159.03, Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64, Docker 29.2.1; shared with the factory-live stack (6 resident CUDA processes, 13 containers); reachable only over Tailscale 100.103.58.32.

facts.subject: bling host
facts.fact: bling (manuel@bling.local, DGX Spark): GB10, driver 580.178.04, freshly installed and idle; host of KILN-002's C4/PN runs, the KILN-002 Kiln server (executor spark) and the KILN-003 driver.

duplications.title: Perf Lab app: kiln lab-workbench vs Playback ML-PERF-001 experiments/lab-workbench
duplications.description: The whole Perf Lab tree exists in two repositories, byte-identical (diff -rq empty); Kiln's copy is a frozen reference never edited after 92daa13, and KILN-002 treats it as untouchable, which is why PE is blocked.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Pick one home. Once @kiln/lab, /api/lab and the KILN-003 kinds cover what Kiln needs, delete Kiln's copy or replace it with a pinned reference (git submodule or recorded revision).

duplications.title: lab language compiler: lab-workbench/src/lang vs packages/lab/src/lang
duplications.description: KILN-001 Phase 8a ported Perf Lab's language into @kiln/lab: three files rewritten on @kiln/evidence, 'everything else was edited in place', differing 'only mechanically'; check:pl proves equivalence against Perf Lab's own code.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Retire lab-workbench/src/lang once nothing builds from it; keep check:pl only while both exist.

duplications.title: lab capture hash cyrb53: lab-workbench, packages/lab and packages/exec
duplications.description: Perf Lab's cyrb53 capture hash has bodies in three lab-related places (plus Kiln's own cyrb53 hash in packages/kiln/src/core/util.js for unrelated keys); KILN-001 D3 and KILN-003 §12.2 both planned to retire it, 8276bf7 moved it into @kiln/exec instead; a normal-form mismatch between copies caused 877c273.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Make packages/exec/src/lab-hash.ts the only lab-hash implementation and import it from @kiln/lab; separately decide whether lab_hash survives at all next to the SHA-256 kiln-capture/1 id.

duplications.title: Perf Lab server modules: lab-workbench/server vs apps/server/src/lab
duplications.description: KILN-001 Phase 8c ported Perf Lab's tar reader 'unchanged except for noUncheckedIndexedAccess' and its store, datasets and evidence modules onto lab_* tables in Kiln's server.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Same as the language: once Kiln's server is the only lab server, delete the lab-workbench server or keep it only as an import source.

duplications.title: Perf Lab data: lab-workbench/.data/perf-lab.sqlite vs Kiln lab tables
duplications.description: lab:import copies Perf Lab's store into Kiln's database and data dir (1 dataset, 1 archive, 128 media, 70 artifacts, 80 runs, 12 jobs) from a temporary copy of db + WAL; both stores then hold the same evidence.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Treat the import as one-way and freeze the Perf Lab store (immutable copy, as K1D09:485-486 suggests).

duplications.title: synthetic host capability reports: lab-workbench/src/data vs packages/lab/src/data
duplications.description: The synthetic GB10 and RTX PRO 6000 capability reports and the synthetic run generator exist in both the Perf Lab copy and @kiln/lab, though KILN-003 plans their removal (P4).
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Do KILN-003 P4: remove synthetic hosts and seeding from @kiln/lab.

duplications.title: kiln_launch.py vendored into Playback redaction
duplications.description: Playback's redaction service vendors Kiln's Python launcher byte-identical below a three-line header (sha256 94a0f717… at Kiln 7bcfc06), excluded from ruff/mypy and guarded by a hash test; it was re-vendored once (ac835daa9) after a launcher fix.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Keep vendoring (the consumer must not depend on Kiln at runtime) but publish the launcher as a versioned artifact so re-vendoring is a version bump.

duplications.title: Kiln launcher and program sets vendored into factory-videos
duplications.description: factory-videos vendors kiln/launch.ts and the program-set JSON for Example A.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Same as the Python launcher: one published launcher package.

duplications.title: detection matching: Playback compare_ground_truth vs Perf Lab detections.ts
duplications.description: ML-PERF-002 ported PR 1005's Python matching rules to TypeScript and pins equivalence by a golden test ('the golden test is the enforcement seam').
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Keep the golden test; drop the lab-workbench copy with the rest of the language.

duplications.title: lab preset metadata: LAB_META vs PRESET_INFO
duplications.description: The workbench kept its own LAB_META list of lab presets beside @kiln/lab's PRESET_INFO until 31b769f made PRESET_INFO the one registry.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Resolved; listed because it shows the copy pattern recurring.

duplications.title: KILN-002 C4 scripts restate validate_on_host start_arm
duplications.description: c4-diag.sh re-states validate_on_host.sh's start_arm mounts and environment; the fallback target spec is constructed in both cuda-runner-smoke.mjs and gb10-spec-check.mjs.

locations.note: 'Same image, mounts and env as validate_on_host.sh's start_arm'

duplications.suggested_consolidation: Ticket scripts; fold into KILN-003 P5 (playback-redaction/1) rather than fix in place.

duplications.title: remote GPU execution: ML-PERF-003 design, KILN-001 executors, KILN-003 driver
duplications.description: Three successive designs of the same mechanism, each superseding the last within days; KILN-003 says 'keeping every existing path would mean keeping three mechanisms behind one interface' and deleted the executors. Only the driver is built now, but SSH reappears as a tunnel outside the core.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Make the tunnel (or Tailscale) part of the host profile so remote reachability has one documented mechanism.
